key_insight: A low-rank LoRA adaptation of SAM3 can efficiently bridge the gap between natural-image pretraining and surgical concept segmentation.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve segmentation support for diagnosis, intraoperative monitoring, and downstream robotic reconstruction or simulation workflows.
method: Inject LoRA adapters into the prompt encoder, detector, and tracker.
Freeze the vision backbone to keep training lightweight.
Optimize only 0.98% of total parameters, enabling single-GPU training.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comprehensive experiments showing the adapted model consistently outperforms zero-shot SAM3 and mainstream baselines.
watch_item: Performance may still depend on surgical data quality and prompt design, and the abstract does not provide dataset size or cross-domain generalization details.
paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of SAM3 for Prompt-Driven Surgical Concept Segmentation
